newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ household net worth rose 0.5 pct in March qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ household net worth rose 0.5 pct in March qtr.

text.p: New Zealand household net worth rose by 0.5 percent over the first quarter of 1997, according to the latest WestpacTrust/FPG houshold savings indicators published on Monday.

"This rise was substantially lower than the 2.7 percent increase recorded over the December 1996 quarter. However, it is typical of the normal savings cycle," said David Beattie, chief investment officer at Westpac Financial Services.
Over the year, households' net worth appreciated by 4.4 percent, which was 2.6 percent above inflation for the same period.
"House prices again played a key role in households' increased wealth, rising 1.9 percent over the quarter," Beattie said.
"However, when household wealth was measured excluding housing assets, households actually experienced a 1.7 percent decline in the financial net worth."
Beattie said decreasing bank deposit levels were the main contributor to households' decline in financial net worth, along with falling share prices.
"It is typical of the normal savings cycle for March quarter savings to be lower. A weaker first quarter is then usually followed by three stronger quarters of savings," Beattie said.

He noted that households were continuing to borrow, although at a slowing rate. An additional NZ$1.1 billion was borrowed by New Zealanders over the quarter, representing a 2.2 percent quarterly increase.
